newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT -Dutch chartists stay neutral on AEX index.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dutch chartists stay neutral on AEX index.

text.p: Dutch chartists mainly stuck to their neutral stance for the week ahead, with some noting that business might be volatile this week and others advising selling any rallies.
"Money flows of the AEX are pointing south, expressing an outflow of funds," said ING Barings, which had opted for the neutral view.
"For the next few days we expect volatile movements starting with a rebound," it added.
During today's session the AEX share index was making up for most of last week's losses as the index rose over nine points in mid-afternoon to nearly 616 points.
The AEX index ended at 606.65 points last Friday, 9.61 points below the 616.26 points on the previous Friday.
Contributor Trend Pvs view Support Resistance

ING BARINGS -- Rising support line around 603 is still intact. Thus crucial support of the AEX at the lower side of its uptrend has been tested twice last week. Though, 603 has been violated on an intraday basis, the AEX closed within the rising trend channel. Support at 603 now looks strong enough to prevent a further slide. Slow momentum of the AEX is still negative, signalling weak underlying technicals. A bearish crossing of two moving average lines (MA14 and MA26) shows also a negative condition. Money flows of the AEX are pointing south, expressing an outflow of funds. For the next few days we expect volatile movements starting with a rebound.

Heavy overhead resistance at 615, then at 622, should cap any rally and limit upward potential. For the short term we remain neutral, but hold on to last week's advise to sell the rallies. A close below 603 would be very negative.

FIBONACCI PRESS -- The intermediate term trend is still up. The short term trend is down as expected, but probably bottoming this week, followed by a new upleg towards early January. Acceleration above 620 and preferably above 629 suggets new all time highs. Before a rally emerges, new lows are possible but not necessary. So, if the correction needs some more time, look for trading between 620 and above 597. Only a sustained move below 589 would open the door for a move to lower support at 580/575.

ABN AMRO -- Many investors are choosing to cash in and this view is exactly in line with our our advice for this week, in which we advise to stay neutral. Due to the high volatile character of the market, there is a high randomness in daily returns. Therefore probability of forecasts remains low. As long as prices don't succeed to break the 615 resistance level, there is still negative potential present in the AEX. First, an intermeiate support lies at 610 and below that we see a short term bottom around 603. In case the index comes that low, we measure downward potential still 572. That level is in our view rock bottom.

On the other hand, if prices break above 615, we would advise to start rebuilding long portfolios carefully. Only if the AEX shows us prices above 624 we find sufficient confidence to focus upwards again.
